questions.markdown: You are developing a smart attendance system for a university. Each class session has a list of student entry times. A student is considered "on time" if they arrive within 5 minutes of the session start time (e.g., session starts at 09:00, on-time arrival is up to 09:05). Develop an algorithm to count how many students arrived on time. The list of arrival times is provided in HH:MM format.

Consider the following non-recursive algorithm:

```text
Algorithm Example1(A[1...n])
    sum = 0
    for i = 1 to n do
        for j = 1 to i do
            sum = sum + A[i] * A[j]
    return sum
```

Analyze the time complexity of this algorithm and express it using Big-O notation, showing the steps of your derivation.

Determine the asymptotic time complexity of the recurrence relations:

i) $T(n)=2T(n/2)+n$

ii) $T(n)=4T(n/2)+n^2$

Consider a sorted array with duplicate elements, e.g., $arr = [2, 5, 5, 5, 8, 12]$. If we use the standard Binary Search code to search for $target = 5$, which index (if any) is guaranteed to be returned? Explain why. How could you modify the Binary Search algorithm to find the first occurrence of the target in such a case? Write an algorithm for this modified approach.

Explain the basic principle of the Brute-Force String Matching algorithm. Illustrate its operation by manually tracing the algorithm to find the pattern **ABA** in the text **CABABABA**. Show the character comparisons made at each step.

How does the performance of Sequential Search change if the array being searched is sorted?
Does sorting the array improve the worst-case time complexity of a standard Sequential Search?
Explain your reasoning with one better algorithm and write the algorithm.

Analyse the worst-case time complexity of Merge sort algorithm considering key comparison as the basic operation. Apply the Merge sort algorithm to the following list to arrange in ascending order:

70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10

and find the total number of key comparisons
